answer: Delayed parent liability queue works by attaching a pigment marker in task logs that ties each new identity to its sponsor. Sponsor rewards are held until the child passes a random audit, and each unverified child adds a spiral of one period to the hold. A failed audit cancels the held reward and sends a ripple through the sponsor’s task eligibility, so creating N clones costs N held rewards plus cooldowns, while passing audits return the hold.
